Key Takeaways

Walmart is rolling out a Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus bundle for $120 annually.

The bundle is almost $100 cheaper than subscribing to both separately.

Customers who already have both may be eligible for a prorated refund.

Walmart is launching a discounted bundle of the retail giant's two memberships as it looks to emphasize value for inflation-weary consumers.

Walmart (WMT) said Tuesday that it is now offering Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus together for $120 a year. That's nearly $100 cheaper than subscribing to both separately, the company said in a release.

The bundle includes free delivery from Walmart and Sam's Club above a certain order size and a choice of an ad-supported version of either Peacock or Paramount+, along with gas discounts and 2% back on certain Sam's Club purchases. For customers who may already have both, the company said most would be eligible for a prorated refund by switching to the new plan.

The move comes as Walmart has looked to enhance its value proposition in recent months as consumers' budgets have been pressured by stubborn inflation. The retailer said it cut prices on thousands of items over the summer, and shares have surged this month as investors weary of the AI trade have rotated into more defensive stocks, including retailers. Walmart said the changes to the program shouldn't impact its third-quarter or full-year forecasts.

Walmart shares were little changed in recent trading, leaving them up about 6% for the year. This month's rally has carried the stock back into positive territory for the year, recovering losses suffered in the wake of Walmart's August report.

title: Walmart gets unexpected boost from stubborn inflation
detail:
Walmart gets unexpected boost from stubborn inflation
Faizan Farooque, Celine Provini
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 11:33 AM MST 7 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For merchants, inflation is often bad news. Walmart (WMT) may be an exception, according to Deutsche Bank.

Analyst Krisztina Katai upgraded Walmart to Buy from Hold and raised her price target to $136 from $113, arguing that stubborn inflation should make Walmart's value proposition more appealing and help it gain market share faster in 2027. The new target implies a 17% upside from the stock level at the time the call was published.

Investing.com reported that Katai expects Walmart's pricing advantage, e-commerce growth, marketplace business, advertising operation, and membership income to reinforce one another as customers become more price-conscious.

For investors and customers alike, time is crucial.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports that while gas prices increased 9.1% in just one month, U.S. consumer prices increased 3.7% in September compared to the same month last year. Despite Walmart's own increased transportation expenses, household budgets are still under pressure due to persistent inflation.

This creates the unique investment case for Deutsche Bank's call: Walmart's customers may become more dependent on the retailer as a result of the same inflation that is squeezing them.

Deutsche Bank says Walmart's price advantage can get stronger

Meetings with Walmart's investor relations team and Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey preceded Katai's elevation.

Management described some of its strongest recent food-market-share gains and continued momentum across e-commerce, marketplace, advertising, and membership, according to Investing.com. Katai also said consumer trends had become stable to somewhat better than they were three months earlier.

The inflation argument is rather simple.

Customers are more motivated to compare costs when household finances are tight. Due to its massive buying power, Walmart is able to maintain lower pricing than many of its smaller rivals while still selling significant amounts of general items, home goods, and food.

That benefit seems quantifiable.

A recent Goldman Sachs grocery survey cited by TheStreet found Walmart's prices were 15.7% below the average of a group that included Kroger, Albertsons, Sprouts Farmers Market, Whole Foods, and Dollar General. Walmart had been 13.7% below the group average only a month earlier, meaning the price gap had widened.

"We see pricing tailwinds building," Katai said, according to Investing.com.

Because Walmart is drawing more customers than those with lower incomes, it is particularly crucial.

What Happened?

Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) launched a $120-a-year membership bundle on Tuesday, which combines Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus.

The company says shoppers save nearly $100 compared with buying the two separately.

The holiday season is coming, and consumer spending is weak as lower- and middle-income households are feeling the pinch.

Walmart, Target and Kroger have all cut prices on thousands of items this year to win over budget-conscious shoppers.

Walmart's own results show the strain. In August, it reported its slowest quarterly comparable sales growth in six years. while average spend per visit also softened from a year ago.

WMT Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

Competition is part of the story too. Membership-only chains like Costco and discount grocers like Aldi have seen stronger traffic in the U.S. Shoppers want convenience and value.

Walmart is also leaning on its advertising platforms to support profits and protect margins.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Walmart Stock

For Walmart stock, the bundle is a way to lock in loyal shoppers as members spend about 4x more than non-members, according to management.

That makes memberships one of the most valuable parts of the business.

The numbers on the last earnings call were solid. Sales grew 5% in constant currency and membership fee revenue rose 17%, an all-time high.

Walmart+ in the U.S. posted double-digit growth, and Sam's Club U.S. membership income grew nearly 6%.

Management also explained the weak comp. U.S. comps rose 2.6%. A change in drug pricing rules cut that figure by 125 basis points. Excluding health and wellness, core categories have stayed in a steady 3% to 4% range.

Walmart stock also benefits from growth beyond stores. E-commerce grew 23% globally, and advertising grew 38%.

Marketplace sales in the U.S. grew 52%, while management said almost half of profit growth came from membership, advertising, and marketplace.

WMT Stock Valuation Model (TIKR)

Management raised guidance but called it a modest raise as it cited more than $2 billion in extra fuel costs and a softer consumer.

It also said Q3 operating income growth would slow to 2% to 4% as it reinvests tariff refunds into lower prices.

So Walmart stock is balancing price cuts against membership growth. Investors in Walmart stock will watch whether the bundle lifts sign-ups this holiday season.

Holiday traffic could also shape how Walmart stock trades.

title: Walmart (WMT): Can Suppliers Keep Funding Its Inventory Growth?

Walmart (WMT): Can Suppliers Keep Funding Its Inventory Growth?
Jeff Lewis
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 6:36 AM MST 5 min read
WMT
TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) benefits from collecting shoppers' cash before many supplier bills fall due. That advantage can finance merchandise growth, but inventory and accounts payable together absorbed approximately $1.0 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027, compared with supplying $0.6 billion a year earlier. Inflation and a larger inventory commitment are testing how efficiently sales become cash.

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) has a forward P/E of approximately 38x versus a trailing P/E of 40x. Operating growth supports the lower forward multiple, while investment revaluations complicate comparisons with reported profit. Management's $2.80–$2.87 adjusted EPS guidance implies 6–9% growth for the year ending January 2027. Target Corporation (NYSE:TGT) guides to 31–44% growth over the comparable fiscal period, but its outlook includes $1.65 per share of tariff refunds. Adjusted earnings can still contain exceptional benefits.

For Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT), Target Corporation (NYSE:TGT) is the closer general-merchandise comparison. Greater purchasing scale, grocery frequency, and growing advertising income support a quality premium. Costco Wholesale Corporation (NASDAQ:COST), at 40x forward earnings, uses a membership warehouse model, making the cost of rewarding customer loyalty part of the comparison. A modest discount to that business does not establish cheapness. The valuation looks demanding unless recurring free cash flow improves.

Read the full comparison here: Costco (COST) vs. Walmart (WMT): Which Retailing Giant Has a Wider Moat?

What Walmart’s (WMT) Dividend Track Record Signals for NYSE Dividend Stocks
Supplier Funding Works Best When Shelves Turn Quickly

Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) ended July with $64.3 billion of accounts payable against $61.6 billion of inventory. Purchasing scale and frequent grocery purchases help merchandise move before suppliers require payment. Reliable availability reinforces customer traffic, while a broad store network spreads distribution costs across substantial sales. These advantages can reduce the capital shareholders must supply for growth.

For Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT), however, a favorable balance-sheet position did not mean inventory funded growth during the half. Inventory changes consumed $2.660 billion of operating cash, while higher payables supplied $1.648 billion. Those cash-flow movements, rather than simply subtracting period-end balances, establish the $1.012 billion drag. As with customer funding that supports production before delivery, payment timing provides financing, not an additional profit margin.
